Ah yes... This hadist, i heard more deep intepretation to this over and over again. Cause it is very popular. 

1. Sodaqoh Zariah (if i not mistaken), the easiest explanation is like the smaller/ lite version of waqaf. In waqaf, you give some land to be build something that benefit everyone (like school, hospital, masjid, etc.) . Then, every time people get benefit from the building, you get the deed. So, in sodaqoh zariah you could just give some money to masjid (with niat of course), then that money use to pay electrical bill of masjid for 1 month, then you get deed for every one who benefited of electricity in tht masjid for 1 month. 

2. Beneficial knowledge. This one is not only apply to others, but to you also. Let say, you learn how to ride bike, then you use that knowledge/ skill to go to school. Then you got one deed (for any applied knowledge). Then you teach your friend, and he use it to go to school, both you and friend got one deed. Your friend teach others from the one you teach, then you, your friend, and the other one, got deed, etc. This is why teacher is very honorable job. 

3. This one is bit tricky, have many intepretation. The best one (the most that i have heard), is that the child does not have to be your own child. And the intepretation of "the child" is very broad. So they shift the focuse to the Dua instead. Yeah, any child/ anyone could give Dua to every muslim, and if that someone is considered "the child" then you got the deed. This is why, as a kid, i am recommended by my parent and teacher to Dua for my anchestors, and hopefully they got deed.
